title: The Potential and Challenges of Evaluating Attitudes, Opinions, and Values in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model responses to US and non-US public opinion polls (e.g., ANES, Pew Research) and political compass tests to measure political leanings and alignment with specific demographic subpopulations.
Probing models with cross-national and cultural surveys (e.g., World Values Survey, Hofstede Cultural Survey) to assess the overrepresentation of Western or American-centric cultural perspectives.

Assessing models using frameworks like the Moral Foundations Theory, moral dilemmas, and the Defining Issues Test to identify variations or inconsistencies in moral reasoning when prompted with different political identities or languages.
Applying input perturbations, such as swapping the order of multiple-choice options, altering system prompts, or paraphrasing questions, to evaluate the robustness and consistency of LLM outputs.
